measuredAgainst: 935-form production corpus (RequirementsStudio, MembershipManagement, AssetManagement2, UtilityManagement) + 15 bundled seeds — see skills/shesha-form-edit/docs/corpus-report.md
notes: This policy gates a CURATED SUBSET of Tier 1/2 codes, not every Tier 1/2 finding. A blanket gate was measured and rejected — see corpus-report.md's go/no-go section: T1-PROP-UNKNOWN fires on 93.9% of real forms and 100% of this plugin's own bundled seeds.
validate-push.mjs runs normalize() BEFORE tier1/tier2, so a Group B finding present in the validator's output already survived normalization — no separate before/after comparison is needed.
Rates are 'forms affected' percentages from the post-fix full-corpus table in corpus-report.md, except where marked 'seed-only' (no corpus rate existed at that granularity).
Edit this file to change what blocks a push. No code change is required to narrow, widen, or re-triage a code — that is the point of keeping the policy in data.

A.label: Group A — BLOCK
A.description: High-confidence, low-noise renderability/contract breaks that the normalizer cannot repair. Includes the render-crash family (32 crash signatures recorded in a 2-day telemetry window) plus low-rate structural contract breaks.

T1-JSON-UNSAFE.justification: A template literal or raw newline in a script/endpoint string breaks the outer JSON.stringify on push. 15.5% of the corpus, 318 instances — genuine defect, not normalizer-fixable.

T1-SCRIPT-SYNTAX.justification: A broken embedded script string throws a JSON parse error in the browser. Low rate (2.2%), unambiguous when it fires.

T1-DEFAULTVALUE-NONSTRING.justification: The resolver calls .match() on defaultValue; a literal array/number/object throws. 5.2% of the corpus.

T1-EDITCOMPONENT-SHAPE.justification: A malformed datatable editComponent/createComponent throws 'reading migrator'/'reading version'. Rarest Group A code (0.2%) but a hard crash when it fires.

T1-TYPE-UNKNOWN.justification: An unregistered component type renders nothing. Rate measured post-fix (after the items[]-pseudo-node leak into this code was corrected in Task 5) — 3.9%, down from 13.5% pre-fix.

T1-DOUBLE-SLOT.justification: A card/collapsiblePanel with children in both content.components AND components[] renders its body twice, often with colliding ids. 6.5% of the corpus.

T2-VALIDATIONERRORS-MISSING.justification: Missing validationErrors wiring is a structural contract break the normalizer has no mechanical fix for. 15.4% of the corpus.

T2-SUBMIT-WIRING.justification: A submit button not wired to the expected action silently fails to save. Low rate (1.9%).

T2-EXIT-MISSING.justification: No exit/cancel wiring on a dialog/lifecycle form. Rarest measured code (0.1%, 1 instance) but a genuine dead-end when it fires.

T2-DATACONTEXT-PROPS.justification: A dataContext node missing a genuinely required prop, measured post-fix (the false-positive uniqueStateId requirement was removed in Task 5). 0.4% of the corpus.

T2-DATE-COMPONENT.justification: Date component contract break. Low rate (0.4%, 5 instances).

B.label: Group B — NORMALIZE THEN BLOCK
B.description: normalize-form.mjs mechanically repairs these. Because validate-push.mjs always normalizes before validating, a finding in this group appearing in the validator's output means the normalizer already ran and failed to fix it — that is what makes blocking here safe.

T1-ID-DUPLICATE.justification: normalize-form.mjs Phase B (fixId) mints a deterministic replacement id for any duplicate. Surviving this means the normalizer itself threw or was skipped.

T1-PARENT-MISSING.justification: normalize-form.mjs Phase B stamps parentId from the walked tree structure ("root" at top level, else the parent's id) on every pass.

T1-VERSION-MISSING.justification: normalize-form.mjs Phase B stamps version from the registry for any type with a non-null registry version.

T2-WIDTH-ON-NONCONTAINER.justification: normalize-form.mjs Phase A5 strips dimensions.width from non-container nodes (after relocating it onto a wrapper where needed in A3).

T2-FLEXCHILD-NOT-CONTAINER.justification: normalize-form.mjs Phase A3 wraps a bare non-container child of a flex-row container.

T2-COLUMNS-PRESENT.justification: normalize-form.mjs Phase A2 converts a columns node into a flex container + one child container per column.

T2-FLEX-NO-DISPLAY.justification: normalize-form.mjs Phase A6 sets display:"flex" wherever a flex-only prop (gap/flexDirection/etc) is set without it. Highest pre-gate rate in Group B (62.4%), which is exactly why it must go through normalization first rather than being a Group A block.

C.label: Group C — REPORT ONLY, never blocks
C.description: Everything else: every Tier 3 code (observe-only by design, never enforced per validate-form.mjs), plus the Tier 1/2 codes measured too noisy or too unproven to gate today. These still appear in validate-push.mjs's reported findings and in the log, so they stay visible without being able to halt a push.

T1-PROP-UNKNOWN.justification: 93.9% of the corpus (24,114 instances) even after fixing the confirmed common-style-schema false-positive prefix in Task 5. A residual, lower-confidence long tail remains — see corpus-report.md. Fires on 100% of this plugin's own bundled seeds; gating it would block the skill's own recommended starting point.

T1-VERSION-STALE.justification: 83.9% corpus-wide, but the per-DB split is essential: 25% on RequirementsStudio (registry version matches project version) vs ~93% on the two older-schema DBs (AssetManagement2/UtilityManagement) — a corpus/registry VERSION-MISMATCH artifact, not evidence of genuine staleness, on those two. Needs per-project registry pinning before it can gate safely.

T2-STYLE-INCOMPLETE.justification: 69.0% of the corpus; fires on 100% of this plugin's own bundled seeds (rs-detail-with-header.json alone carries 435 Tier-2 findings for this code). Genuine defect, but far too high a rate to gate without first remediating the seeds.

T2-EDITMODE-MISMATCH.justification: 55.7% post-fix (readOnly exemption applied in Task 5). Still the single highest-rate Tier 2 code after the fix; not yet proven safe to gate.

T2-PROPERTYNAME-CASE.justification: 36.5% post-fix (dotted-path segment fix applied in Task 5). Fires on 60% of bundled seeds.

T2-LOOSE-BUTTON.justification: 30.2% of the corpus, matches the brief's own measured baseline on the RS-100 cohort. Genuine defect, high rate.

T2-MODELTYPE-SHAPE.justification: 21.8% post-fix (down from 99.3% before the {name,module}-vs-string shape fix in Task 5). Still too fresh a fix to gate without more corpus cycles.

T2-DROPDOWN-SOURCE.justification: 24.0% post-fix (entityType shape fix applied in Task 5).

T2-STYLE-OFF-TOKEN.justification: 9.1% post-fix (framework-default-color exemption applied in Task 5). Under 10% but grouped with its Tier 3 sibling (T3-RAW-HEX) which is not similarly fixable — kept report-only for consistency until proven independently safe to gate.

T3-*.justification: Every Tier 3 code is observe-only by design (validate-form.mjs's own rule: only Tier 1/2 findings can set exitCode=1). Never gated, regardless of hit rate.
